reason: Accepting the fixture's self-signed certificate for a persistent context (`ignoreHTTPSErrors`). A launched default context takes no creation options, so its TLS origins can't be reached as the original reaches them (defaultbrowsercontext-2's DC-021 has the same gap)

Accepting a self-signed HTTPS certificate in a context (`ignoreHTTPSErrors`), which these tests need for their TLS origins. Chromium refuses `acceptInsecureCerts` with Unsupported, because its certificate override applies to the whole browser (as browsercontext-add-cookies' CO-041 does)
The test writes a cookie from inside a cross-site frame, which needs the frame's `evaluate` in its isolated world. Stock WebKit has no isolated worlds (`isolatedWorlds` is unsupported)
The original skips Firefox over BiDi, where its Total Cookie Protection blocks this third-party cookie
The original skips WebKit, which has no third-party cookies
The original is test.fixme for WebKit on Linux, so it states no expectation there to port
